steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The subjunctive mood expresses possibility, purpose, wish, or subordinate action — unlike the indicative, which states facts.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Present subjunctive is formed by changing the stem vowel: 1st conjugation changes -a- to -e- (muset), 2nd changes -e- to -ea- (moneas), 3rd/4th change to -a- (ducamus, audiamus).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Imperfect subjunctive is formed by adding -re to the infinitive: laudarem (I would praise / I might praise).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Purpose clauses: ut + subjunctive = 'in order to' (positive); ne + subjunctive = 'in order not to' (negative). Example: venit ut pater videret (he came in order that his father might see).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: How does the present subjunctive differ from the indicative in the 1st and 3rd conjugations? | Q: How is the imperfect subjunctive formed? | Q: What is the difference between a purpose clause and a result clause?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 1st conjugation: the stem vowel changes from -a- to -e- (e.g. laudem, not laudo). 3rd conjugation: the stem vowel changes to -a- (e.g. ducam, not duco). The 2nd changes -e- to -ea- (moneam), and the 4 | Add -re to the present infinitive (second principal part). Example: laudare + -re → laudarem (I would/might praise). The imperfect subjunctive is the same for all conjugations. | Purpose clause: ut/ne + subjunctive = 'in order to/not to'. Result clause: ut + subjunctive after tam/tantus/ita = 'so...that'. Purpose gives the intention; result gives the outcome.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When you see ut + subjunctive, always check for tam/tantus/ita in the main clause to determine if it is purpose or result. Learn the subjunctive forms of sum and possum — they appear very frequently in set texts. For cum clauses, translate all three possibilities (when/since/although) and choose the one that makes best sense in context. The imperfect subjunctive is easy to recognise: it looks like the infinitive with personal endings (laudarem, laudares, laudaret).
